newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends little changed, seen range-bound.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends little changed, seen range-bound.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed little changed on Thursday and dealers said it was range-bound, looking to dollar/yen for its next move.
The currency ended at US$0.7058/63 and 67.36 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7053/60 and 67.35 at the opening, after trading a 0.7048-62 range on the day.

A Wellington dealer said there was little immediate focus on politics, where coalition talks between nationalist New Zealand First and the main National and Labour parties look set to drag on for some weeks after an inconclusive general election.
He said there seemed to be plenty of kiwi/yen interest. One school of thought was that a dollar/yen break below 113.60 would take the kiwi lower, while a rise in the dollar would push it higher.
"I think we could be trapped in some pretty narrow ranges for a couple of days until something happens one way or the other," he said.

Government fiscal figures for the three months to September, due on Friday, are seen as historical and unlikely to excite the market. An Auckland dealer said that barring sharp movements in interest rates, politics were likely to provide the main
influence until the Reserve Bank issues its next Monetary Policy Statement on December 17. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
